# PRD 007: starting and stopping a seat in a role

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 007-role-start.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

<a id="meta"></a>

## Meta

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| title | PRD 007: starting and stopping a seat in a role |
| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-25 |
| owner | pm-001 |
| summary | Spawning a seat with a role named on it gives a registered seat that has already been told what it needs, so nobody rewrites the same brief. Any seat can create the seat the work needs, and the prime is told. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Starting a role holder takes three manual steps today: spawn, `pij directory assign`, then send the seat its packet by hand. The role records a model, but pij does not apply it, so the prime passes it again at spawn. A seat can also be spawned and never assigned, and it then runs with no role on record: on 2026-11-24 the pij fleet's own prime counted about five such seats. Primes re-create near-identical roles and briefs for each new subject because nothing fills in the parts that differ. Nothing obliges a seat that finds an area nobody owns to say so, so new experts appear only when the prime happens to notice.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Be asked about a new long-lived seat only when the prime is unsure, and see every seat that exists. |
| a-prime | prime | Start a seat in a role in one step, and add what this run is about without restating the rest. |
| a-seat | any seat | Create the seat the work needs, or flag an area with no owner, without waiting for permission. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | A prime starts a role holder with one command and writes only what is specific to this run. |
| g-2 | No seat the prime creates runs without a role on record. |
| g-3 | When an expert is missing, whoever notices can create it, and the prime always knows what exists. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | Groups of seats started together. That is PRD 008 (pods). |
| n-2 | Changing how job packets are sent after a seat has started. `pij send role:&lt;id&gt; --body-file` is unchanged. |
| n-3 | Approval gates on creating seats. pij records and informs; it does not police who may create what. |

| req-12 | Closing a seat can really take it down | There is one way to take a seat down: `pij close`. Today it gives a role holder a memory turn and then only marks the seat closed, leaving its process running for someone to stop by hand. With `--stop` it also asks the seat to answer ready once its memory is written, then stops the exact process pij recorded when it launched the seat, never by name or pattern. A seat that does not answer in time, or answers with no memory note, is left running and the prime is told which seat and why. A cold seat is not woken: pij warns with what waking it would cost, stops it without waking if it already has a memory note, and otherwise leaves it and tells the prime. Without `--stop`, close behaves as it does today. | prime | must | [x] shipped | `pij close &lt;seat&gt; --stop` on a warm holder leaves a memory note, no running process and a closed seat; on a silent seat it leaves the process running and the prime gets one message naming it; on a cold seat it sends nothing and prints the wake price; `pij close &lt;seat&gt;` with no flag behaves as before. | operator, 2026-11-25: taking down a single seat follows the same rules as a pod; holders answer ready first, the prime is told if they don't, and cold seats are warned about | — | — |
